clue.text: Several getting by, supported by deliveries repeatedly

indicators.note: in a down entry, something supported by another part sits on top of it, so the earlier words come first

blocks.note: several and many are synonyms
by as in multiplication: three by four is three times four
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

explanation.surface: Several parcels keep arriving, the deliveries piling up on the doorstep again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler's deliveries are grouped in sixes called overs. In a down answer the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a great number of times means doing it again and again, which is what repeatedly expresses.

clue.text: Finally trek leader follows maps in a book

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept
one piece following another means it is placed after it in the answer

blocks.note: an atlas is a bound collection of maps
the first letter of trek

explanation.surface: At the end of the day, the hiking leader checks the route in a printed book of maps.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something happening after a long wait, a synonym of finally.

clue.text: With a flourish, shows a selection of fibre-rich food offerings

blocks.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain, eaten for its fibre
dishes are items of food offered on a menu

explanation.surface: A health-food café proudly displays its range of high-fibre meals.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave something about dramatically for display is a flourishing kind of showing off, the verb's core sense.

clue.text: Film studio ultimately competes in cinema

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes at the very end, so each of the two words before it gives its final letter

blocks.note: the last letters of film and of studio
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: A film studio ends up competing for audiences in the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like the definition, but it is one of the two words that 'ultimately' trims to a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the movies is the American idiom for going to the cinema; both name the film industry and its screenings.

clue.text: Powerless to accept the Guardian is not fit for purpose

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: powerless means lacking the ability
the newspaper setting the puzzle refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A complaint that a feeble refusal to take the Guardian seriously makes something useless.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle appears in the Guardian, so the paper's name stands for us, the publisher speaking of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be put to use fails to serve its intended function, the plain meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Descartes has a disfigurement

indicators.note: the name has the letters within it, held inside its spelling

blocks.note: letters three to six of the philosopher's name

explanation.surface: The French philosopher is said to bear a mark on his face.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left on the skin by a healed wound is a common example of a blemish that spoils appearance.

clue.text: Allowed to carry thin glove

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that carries another holds it up from below, so the carried piece comes first

blocks.note: gaunt means thin and bony
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to wear a thin glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin glove' reads as one phrase, but the adjective belongs to the wordplay. In a down clue the carrier is at the bottom, so it is written last.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong protective covering for the hand with a flared cuff, worn by knights and motorcyclists, is a type of glove.

clue.text: Green fare movement encourages food products compatible with animal welfare

definitions.text: food products compatible with animal welfare

indicators.note: movement suggests letters shifting position into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words
to egg someone on is to encourage them

explanation.surface: An environmental food campaign promotes produce from farms that treat animals well.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs from hens allowed to roam outdoors are sold as the humane choice for shoppers concerned about livestock conditions.

clue.text: PM seen in a newspaper with the Queen and now gone, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letters of each preceding word are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
FT is the Financial Times
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina
the middle letters of and, now and gone

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister appeared in the press beside the late Queen, now gone.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is the time abbreviation post meridiem. The Financial Times is a London daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation post meridiem marks hours after midday, which covers this part of the day.

clue.text: Professor could be rocking

blocks.note: first meaning: a professorship, or the person holding one
second meaning: a seat, one kind of which rocks back and forth

explanation.surface: An academic might be having a great time, or perhaps teetering.
explanation.definitionFit: A university chair is a professorial post, and a rocking chair is a seat on curved runners.

clue.text: Declare why make money for long

indicators.note: to declare is to say out loud, so the word is taken by how it is pronounced

blocks.note: the letter Y is pronounced like the question word
to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: Someone asks aloud why anyone would spend so long making money.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to want it intensely, and the verb here is a direct synonym of that desire.

clue.text: In case, run out and find cover

indicators.note: out suggests the words are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters of both words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to get a policy just in case your luck runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' and 'cover' together make a neat sentence about protection, which hides that the first three words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy protecting against loss is commonly called cover in British usage.

clue.text: Mash of poorest quality, but not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: tatty means shabby or of poor quality; this is its superlative

explanation.surface: The mashed potato is the worst you could get, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatties is a Scottish word for potatoes, served mashed in the dish neeps and tatties.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is mashed potato, and the Scottish word for potatoes stands for it by close association.

clue.text: See 1
Criminal destruction of half of Salzburg cellar

indicators.note: destroying half of each word means the front portion is removed, leaving its second half

blocks.note: the Austrian city, whose second half is kept
taken as written, then halved

explanation.surface: A vandal wrecks half of a wine cellar in Salzburg.
explanation.definitionFit: A housebreaker who enters premises to steal is a particular kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Trained in secret as underground opposition

indicators.note: something trained is shaped or drilled into a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters of both words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fighters drilled covertly to form a clandestine opposition movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' does double duty in the surface but is part of the letters to rearrange; nothing joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert groups fighting an occupying power, such as in wartime France, are known as the movement of that name.

clue.text: See 8
Demonstration of the month

blocks.note: first meaning: a protest procession
second meaning: the third month of the year

explanation.surface: A protest is named as the standout event of its month.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest walk through the streets is called by this name, which is also the calendar's third month.

clue.text: Helping a learner to be sensible

blocks.note: a ration is a portion or helping
taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate in Britain

explanation.surface: Assisting a student in order to be reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' reads as a verb but is the noun, a serving of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Being guided by reason and logic is what makes someone level-headed and sound in judgement.

clue.text: Grant sound and colour

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by pronunciation, not spelling

blocks.note: Hugh Grant is the English film actor

explanation.surface: A grant that is financially sound, and colourful too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant sound' reads as a sound grant of money; Grant is the surname of actor Hugh Grant, whose first name is the sound wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade or tint is a hue, the standard synonym for a particular colour.

clue.text: For a start, how are you feeling? Always sneezing?

definitions.note: a symptom standing for the condition that causes it

indicators.note: a start is the beginning, so each word in the question gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letters of how, are, you and feeling
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A doctor asks a patient how they feel, noting they never stop sneezing.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy to pollen, whose hallmark symptom is constant sneezing, is identified here by that symptom.

clue.text: Was there to observe material

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: attended as an onlooker, as when someone sits in on a class
second meaning: a smooth glossy fabric

explanation.surface: Someone attended in order to watch some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit in on a meeting is to attend without taking part, and the glossy fabric shares the letters.

clue.text: Meet, for example, grabbing fist somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged
grabbing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: say is used to introduce an example
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people meet and one grabs the other's fist in a clumsy greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a demand or requirement is to fulfil it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Juliet in same but different fragrance

indicators.note: different means changed from its original form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Juliet wears the same perfume, yet it smells different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it is simply two of the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet-scented flower is a popular perfume note, so it serves as a kind of scent.

clue.text: Carpenter with a coat of many colours?

definitions.text: with a coat of many colours

blocks.note: first meaning: the carpenter of Nazareth, husband of Mary in the Gospels

blocks.clueFragment: with a coat of many colours
blocks.note: second meaning: the son of Jacob in Genesis, given a richly coloured coat

explanation.surface: A woodworker in a brightly painted jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Two biblical figures share the name: Mary's husband who worked with wood, and Jacob's favourite son.

clue.text: Press pitch regularly ignored, which is funny

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals means every other letter is dropped

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
the second and fourth letters of pitch

explanation.surface: A sales pitch that the press keeps overlooking, which is amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests journalists, but it is the household task done with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny in the sense of wryly odd: a situation that turns out contrary to expectation is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Euros sold out as nothing to be sniffed at

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The currency has sold out, which is no trivial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing to be sniffed at' is an idiom meaning not to be scorned; read literally, it is something with no smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no scent means there is literally nothing for the nose to detect, the literal reading of the idiom.

clue.text: See 1
Woman showing compassion in a Beirut hotel

indicators.note: in means contained within the following words, running across them

blocks.note: the end of the city's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A kind woman helps people in a hotel in the Lebanese capital.
explanation.walkthrough: As a common noun the word means compassion, now rare outside ruthless; the biblical Ruth is famed for her loyalty to Naomi.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name that is also an old word for pity, so the woman embodies kindness.

clue.text: Home poetry by sailor

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A sailor writes verse about home.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where someone lives is their dwelling, a formal synonym for a residence.

clue.text: See 8
Strictly accurate cutback by court

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the word before it runs right to left

blocks.note: the cut part of the word: to axe something is to cut it; the rest of the word signals the turnaround
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A court rules precisely on a spending reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutback' looks like one noun, a spending reduction, but it splits into a word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and correct in every detail, with no approximation, is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Anticipating being in the club

blocks.note: first meaning: looking forward to
second meaning: British slang for pregnant, short for in the pudding club

explanation.surface: Looking forward to becoming a member of the club.
explanation.walkthrough: In the club is informal British slang for pregnant, which this word also means.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting for something to happen is anticipating it, and a woman carrying a baby is said to be pregnant.
